title: Multitenant interference prober and kernel-attribution exporter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a synthetic multitenant interference prober and an exporter that correlates latency spikes with kernel-level attribution; useful as a new baseline for variance and regression tests.
description: Motivation: We observed recurring, low-amplitude latency tails in multi-tenant experiments that are poorly explained by request-level telemetry alone; root causes often live in kernel scheduling/driver contention and cross-tenant interference. This PR introduces a lightweight, deterministic multitenant interference prober and a pipeline that enriches benchmark traces with kernel-attribution markers so we can systematically reproduce and attribute tail events. What this change does: implements a bench harness (bench/probers/interference_prober.go + python runner) that spins configurable co-tenants with adjustable CPU/IO pressure profiles; adds a kotlin-compatible exporter (bench/exporters/kernel_attribution_exporter.{py,md}) that annotates traces with coarse kernel events (irq, scheduler_slice, cgroup_migrations) sampled via eBPF shim and aggregates them to token-level latency buckets; supplies a profiling baseline and an example runbook (bench/recipes/multitenant_interference_baseline.yaml) and a small dashboard template for the observability team. Determinism: prober supports seedable RNG for request timings and has an optional fixed-prime warmup sequence to stabilize KV cache states. Outputs: per-run JSON with per-quantile attribution summaries, a compact pprof flame-annotated tarball, and a CSV summary for comparison across runs. Backcompat and safety: the prober runs in a user-space container and only enables eBPF collection when the host allows it; all exporters gracefully fall back to synthetic attribution tags when kernel events are unavailable. How to run: see bench/README.md addition that documents a one-line invocation and an optional --compare flag to diff against a stored baseline. Why unique: unlike our existing workload runners this harness focuses on correlated cross-tenant interference patterns and couples per-token latency histograms with kernel-sourced signals to accelerate triage and regression detection. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the prober light-weight (no long-running cluster changes) and includes CI smoke tests that run the harness at reduced scale in our Linux runner. Related work: builds on ideas from ENG-1190 (kv-warmup) and ENG-1367 (tail-attribution proto).
commits: 3 commits: 1) add interference prober harness and lightweight runner; 2) implement kernel attribution exporter and example dashboard; 3) tests, docs, and CI smoke harness adjustments.
